development area: Digital asset discovery and inventory navigation
description: Ability to search, interpret, and assess enterprise data inventories, system catalogues, repositories, and reusable processing components before proposing new development.
historic work: Key Activities - Develops processing systems and applications used to manipulate, store and retrieve statistical data.
change to work: This activity would no longer begin directly with development. It would be updated to include a mandatory pre-development stage in which the officer scans existing enterprise data assets, systems, and reusable digital tools to determine whether requirements can be met without creating a new solution. Development work would proceed only after documented justification and feasibility review.
justification: The current work-description emphasizes development and implementation but does not explicitly require systematic discovery of existing assets before building new solutions.

description: Ability to compare reuse, enhancement, automation, and net-new development options and document why the selected approach is operationally justified.
historic work: Key Activities - Develops processing systems and applications used to manipulate, store and retrieve statistical data.
change to work: This activity would no longer begin directly with development. It would be updated to include a mandatory pre-development stage in which the officer scans existing enterprise data assets, systems, and reusable digital tools to determine whether requirements can be met without creating a new solution. Development work would proceed only after documented justification and feasibility review.
justification: The future expectation requires stronger early-stage justification for whether a new system is necessary.

development area: AI and automation applicability in statistical operations
description: Knowledge of where AI, rules-based automation, and digital workflow tools can substitute for or augment manual or custom-built processing solutions.
historic work: Key Activities - Develops processing systems and applications used to manipulate, store and retrieve statistical data.
change to work: This activity would no longer begin directly with development. It would be updated to include a mandatory pre-development stage in which the officer scans existing enterprise data assets, systems, and reusable digital tools to determine whether requirements can be met without creating a new solution. Development work would proceed only after documented justification and feasibility review.
justification: The update explicitly requires consideration of AI and automation capabilities from the outset, which is not stated in the current role.

development area: Federated data sourcing and enterprise data reuse
description: Knowledge of internal and external data source ecosystems, reusable administrative or survey assets, and how federated sources can satisfy emerging requirements.
historic work: Key Activities - Assesses changes in the subject area and determines the need to modify or replace processing systems and applications for the manipulation, storage and retrieval of statistical data
change to work: Assessment of change would expand beyond subject-area developments to include whether existing enterprise assets, federated data sources, automation tools, and digital workflows can address the change. The threshold for recommending replacement or modification becomes more rigorous and evidence-based.
justification: The current wording focuses on subject-area change and system implications, but not on enterprise asset reuse or federated sourcing.

description: Ability to evaluate whether changes should be addressed through system replacement, process redesign, automation, or integration with existing digital workflows.
historic work: Key Activities - Assesses changes in the subject area and determines the need to modify or replace processing systems and applications for the manipulation, storage and retrieval of statistical data
change to work: Assessment of change would expand beyond subject-area developments to include whether existing enterprise assets, federated data sources, automation tools, and digital workflows can address the change. The threshold for recommending replacement or modification becomes more rigorous and evidence-based.
justification: The role must distinguish between a true need for replacement and a need that can be met through workflow redesign or automation.

development area: Structured intake and requirements triage facilitation
description: Ability to guide stakeholders through standardized needs-identification steps, including problem framing, asset review, reuse analysis, and feasibility gating.
historic work: Key Activities - Provides subject matter advice and direction to users, negotiates procedural modifications and establishes project plans, priorities and target dates.
change to work: Advice to users will increasingly need to challenge assumptions that new requirements require new systems or collections. The officer will need to guide users through a standardized intake and needs-identification process, including evidence from asset scans, feasibility criteria, and enterprise constraints before project planning proceeds.
justification: The future state requires facilitation of a standardized, enterprise-driven needs identification funnel, which goes beyond current advisory and negotiation expectations.

description: Ability to present feasibility, reuse, risk, and cost-benefit findings clearly to users and managers to support intake and governance decisions.
historic work: Key Activities - Provides subject matter advice and direction to users, negotiates procedural modifications and establishes project plans, priorities and target dates.
change to work: Advice to users will increasingly need to challenge assumptions that new requirements require new systems or collections. The officer will need to guide users through a standardized intake and needs-identification process, including evidence from asset scans, feasibility criteria, and enterprise constraints before project planning proceeds.
justification: The role will need to synthesize findings for decision points and negotiate based on documented evidence rather than only procedural preferences.

description: Knowledge of metadata practices, interoperability principles, and standards that enable asset discovery, reuse, and compatibility across systems and programs.
historic work: Key Activities - Participates as a subject area representative on teams and working groups throughout the department.
change to work: Participation would increasingly involve representing not only subject-matter needs but also enterprise reuse, metadata, interoperability, and digital-first feasibility considerations in cross-departmental governance and design forums.
justification: Broader collaboration with enterprise data, architecture, and digital functions is implied but not reflected in the current role framing.

development area: Pre-project governance and gated delivery leadership
description: Ability to lead teams through structured initiation, feasibility review, and evidence-based approval processes before committing to implementation.
historic work: Key Activities - Leads project teams or supervises work units in the development and implementation of new or modified statistical processing systems.
change to work: Leadership would begin earlier in the lifecycle, requiring direction of pre-project reviews, evidence gathering, and feasibility analyses before development approval. Team leadership would incorporate governance checkpoints and documented business rationale, not only implementation planning.
justification: Current leadership expectations focus on execution once work is underway, but future requirements shift leadership upstream into gated assessment and justification.

description: Ability to evaluate requirements using operational, technical, data, automation, cost, risk, and sustainability criteria in an integrated manner.
historic work: Technical Activities - 1. Decision making - Identifies and assesses changes and developments in the subject area; determines the impact on program subject-matter content and the implication for statistical methods and procedures and the dissemination of program results.
change to work: Decision-making would expand from subject-matter implications to include enterprise resource implications, existing data and system availability, AI/automation suitability, and operational sustainability before recommending action.
justification: The future expectation introduces broader dimensions of analysis that are not captured in the current decision frame.

description: Ability to distinguish whether a problem is best addressed through data reuse, metadata improvement, automation, process redesign, integration, or new development.
historic work: Technical Activities - 1. Decision making - Identifies and evaluates problems in the manipulation, storage and retrieval of statistical information to provide solutions or recommendations to management and to resolve subject-matter, conceptual and technical problems referred by staff.
change to work: Problem evaluation would now include determining whether issues can be solved through existing assets, integration, metadata improvements, workflow automation, or process redesign rather than defaulting to system change recommendations.
justification: The current role addresses technical problem solving but not enterprise option-space analysis across data, process, and automation layers.

description: Ability to prepare concise, decision-ready documentation that demonstrates why proposed modifications are necessary and preferable to alternatives.
historic work: Technical Activities - 1. Decision making - Implements enhancements or modifications to processing systems and applications used to manipulate, store and retrieve statistical data.
change to work: Implementation decisions would require stronger documented justification showing that enhancement or modification is preferable to reuse of current assets or adoption of automated or digital alternatives. The officer's discretion becomes more evidence-bound.
justification: The current activity assumes implementation authority following analysis, but future expectations require formal evidence and comparative justification.

development area: Digital product lifecycle and upstream delivery planning
description: Knowledge of how to plan resources and milestones for intake, discovery, feasibility, governance, and implementation as an integrated lifecycle.
historic work: Technical Activities - 2. Leadership and operational management - Leads project teams or work units. Determines goals, priorities and milestones, sets objectives, and plans and schedules the work, resolves conflicting priorities; assesses human resources needs, recommends the appropriate selection methods (internal and external resources / contractors) to meet program objectives, recruits staff, evaluates employee performance, develops training plans, motivates and maintains morale of employees.
change to work: Operational leadership will need to account for new initiation tasks such as digital scanning, metadata review, business intelligence-supported discovery, and formal feasibility documentation. Priorities and staffing may shift toward analytical and discovery capabilities earlier in the project lifecycle.
justification: Future work requires resourcing and planning for enterprise discovery and pre-project analysis tasks not currently foregrounded.

description: Ability to estimate and compare financial, operational, and risk implications of reuse, automation, integration, and new development options.
historic work: Technical Activities - 2. Leadership and operational management - Plans and budgets for special projects, including estimates for salaries, professional fees and implementation costs, with authority to allocate funds within budget. Provides input to budgets based on operational needs and by obtaining/providing cost estimates for personnel, supplies, equipment purchases and travel for use in developing section or division budgets. Procures goods and services within approved budget allocations.
change to work: Budgeting would need to reflect earlier-stage analysis costs and more formal cost-benefit-risk comparisons, including the costs of reuse, integration, automation, and sustainability implications, not just implementation expenditures.
justification: The update explicitly calls for operationalizing cost-benefit-risk analysis at the systems and process design stage.

description: Knowledge of sustainability considerations in digital solution design, including long-term maintainability, duplication avoidance, and operational efficiency.
historic work: Technical Activities - 2. Leadership and operational management - Plans and budgets for special projects, including estimates for salaries, professional fees and implementation costs, with authority to allocate funds within budget. Provides input to budgets based on operational needs and by obtaining/providing cost estimates for personnel, supplies, equipment purchases and travel for use in developing section or division budgets. Procures goods and services within approved budget allocations.
change to work: Budgeting would need to reflect earlier-stage analysis costs and more formal cost-benefit-risk comparisons, including the costs of reuse, integration, automation, and sustainability implications, not just implementation expenditures.
justification: Sustainability perspectives are newly required in feasibility assessment.

description: Ability to elicit needs while testing assumptions against existing assets, constraints, and enterprise standards.
historic work: Technical Activities - 3. Communication - Discusses program subject-matter content requirements with operations managers, other subject matter and systems specialists, clients, service providers and others to comprehend and elaborate the framework and conditions within which statistical development and operations will occur. There is a requirement to understand the issues and resolve differences that can affect the efficiency of the division's operations and quality of outputs.
change to work: These discussions would need to incorporate structured challenge, evidence from digital scans, and feasibility criteria, changing communication from primarily eliciting requirements to jointly validating whether a requirement is already satisfiable through existing capabilities.
justification: The communication function is becoming more analytical and evidence-based at the intake stage.

description: Ability to convert technical discovery, metadata findings, and option analysis into concise recommendations for project approval and prioritization.
historic work: Technical Activities - 3. Communication - Liaises with other subject matter specialists and users to develop and translate subject-matter requirements into specifications for system development, to suggest improvements to ongoing programs, to negotiate procedural modifications and to establish project plans, priorities and target dates. Writes and presents detailed subject matter and technical concepts, definitions and terms in common terminology in order to explain and clarify divisional program content and applications.
change to work: Translation of requirements into specifications would increasingly be preceded by translation into feasibility evidence, asset audit findings, and decision options. The officer would need to communicate why some requests should be met through reuse or process change rather than new development.
justification: The role must increasingly synthesize discovery and feasibility outputs for formal decision points, which is broader than specification writing.

description: Knowledge of metadata models, cataloguing practices, and discovery mechanisms needed to identify, assess, and reuse existing data assets.
historic work: Technical Activities - 4. Knowledge of specialized fields - Knowledge of the concepts, methods and techniques used in the manipulation, storage and retrieval of statistical data in order to coordinate and advise on subject-matter development and resolve subject-matter concept and definition issues.
change to work: Specialized knowledge would need to expand from data handling techniques to include how enterprise data inventories, metadata structures, reusable assets, and federated access models support discovery before new collection or system design.
justification: The current knowledge requirement is operationally focused on handling statistical data, not on discovering and reusing it across the enterprise.

description: Knowledge of how systems, platforms, and workflows integrate across an organization to support scalable, reusable, and interoperable statistical operations.
historic work: Technical Activities - 4. Knowledge of specialized fields - Knowledge of system analysis and design, computer processing, generalized survey software packages to manage the design, development, testing, maintenance and implementation of processing systems; to design specifications for the testing of data, and to maintain and develop databases.
change to work: System analysis and design knowledge would need to incorporate enterprise architecture considerations, interoperability, automation-readiness, digital workflow compatibility, and lifecycle sustainability at the earliest stages of analysis.
justification: The update introduces additional system-design criteria beyond technical design and processing.

description: Knowledge of the organization's broader data, system, and service landscape, including where reusable assets are located and how they can be assessed.
historic work: Technical Activities - 5. Contextual knowledge - Knowledge of statistical programs within Statistics Canada related to the area of expertise in order to identify and select sources of information for development and operations and/or special studies and to identify and evaluate data conflicts.
change to work: Contextual knowledge would broaden from awareness of related statistical programs to practical knowledge of enterprise-wide assets, registries, catalogues, and sources that can be reused before initiating new proposals.
justification: The current requirement acknowledges source identification, but the future state requires more formal and enterprise-wide scanning capability.

description: Ability to systematically compare existing and proposed methods, systems, and processes using documented evaluation criteria and evidence.
historic work: Technical Activities - 6. Research and analysis - Analyzes current manipulation, storage and retrieval methods and procedures to ascertain their relevancy and to determine the need for modification or replacement with alternative systems, methods and procedures.
change to work: This analysis would become more formalized and comparative, requiring documented review of current assets, alternative reuse pathways, automation options, process redesign possibilities, and the risks of duplication before recommending change.
justification: The activity already aligns closely with the update, but future expectations deepen the rigor and documentation standard required.

description: Ability to conduct standardized, enterprise-oriented feasibility studies that incorporate asset audits, automation opportunities, digital workflow fit, and formal recommendation pathways.
historic work: Technical Activities - 6. Research and analysis - Conducts feasibility studies concerning new system and product requirements by examining existing, proposed or new software programs and systems to determine their feasibility and adaptability to the needs of the statistical program.
change to work: Feasibility studies would become broader in scope and earlier in timing. They would include structured scans for existing data assets, formal documentation of inability to meet needs with current assets, AI and automation options, operational sustainability, digital compatibility, and decision-point synthesis for governance.
justification: This is the core activity most directly affected by the update; the current feasibility focus is narrower and more technically bounded.

development area: Business intelligence and discovery tool usage
description: Ability to use dashboards, catalogues, metadata search tools, and other discovery platforms to identify existing data and system assets relevant to a request.
historic work: Technical Activities - 6. Research and analysis - Conducts feasibility studies concerning new system and product requirements by examining existing, proposed or new software programs and systems to determine their feasibility and adaptability to the needs of the statistical program.
change to work: Feasibility studies would become broader in scope and earlier in timing. They would include structured scans for existing data assets, formal documentation of inability to meet needs with current assets, AI and automation options, operational sustainability, digital compatibility, and decision-point synthesis for governance.
justification: The future role requires use of structured digital scanning and business intelligence tools for rapid discovery.

development area: Enterprise digital architecture and interoperability standards
description: Knowledge of organization-wide digital integration principles, interoperability requirements, interface standards, and system alignment criteria needed to assess whether proposed solutions fit enterprise design expectations.
historic work: Key Activities - Assesses changes in the subject area and determines the need to modify or replace processing systems and applications for the manipulation, storage and retrieval of statistical data
change to work: This activity expands from assessing subject-area change impacts to assessing whether any proposed modification or replacement is digitally aligned, interoperable, reusable, automatable, and resource-justified. The officer would be expected to reject or challenge custom/manual approaches unless exceptions are explicitly supported.
justification: The current wording emphasizes subject-area change and system replacement need, but not enterprise digital alignment or reuse-first decision criteria.

development area: Agency data holdings and reuse opportunities
description: Knowledge of existing internal data assets, administrative sources, shared platforms, and reusable services to determine whether new collection, new processing, or custom builds can be avoided.
historic work: Key Activities - Assesses changes in the subject area and determines the need to modify or replace processing systems and applications for the manipulation, storage and retrieval of statistical data
change to work: This activity expands from assessing subject-area change impacts to assessing whether any proposed modification or replacement is digitally aligned, interoperable, reusable, automatable, and resource-justified. The officer would be expected to reject or challenge custom/manual approaches unless exceptions are explicitly supported.
justification: The future expectation requires reuse and automation to be tested at inception, which is not explicit in the current role.

development area: Option analysis using cost-efficiency and resource-justification frameworks
description: Ability to compare manual, custom, reused, and automated options using structured analysis of costs, benefits, constraints, and operational sustainability.
historic work: Key Activities - Assesses changes in the subject area and determines the need to modify or replace processing systems and applications for the manipulation, storage and retrieval of statistical data
change to work: This activity expands from assessing subject-area change impacts to assessing whether any proposed modification or replacement is digitally aligned, interoperable, reusable, automatable, and resource-justified. The officer would be expected to reject or challenge custom/manual approaches unless exceptions are explicitly supported.
justification: The officer must explicitly eliminate or justify manual/custom approaches and weigh resource constraints in early assessments.

description: Ability to design processing solutions that are modular, reusable, automatable, and compatible with enterprise workflows rather than narrowly optimized for a single program.
historic work: Key Activities - Develops processing systems and applications used to manipulate, store and retrieve statistical data.
change to work: System development is no longer only about functional delivery; it must now be designed for reuse, automation, and integration from the beginning. Development work would need to conform to digital-by-default principles and avoid isolated or bespoke solutions where standard components exist.
justification: Current expectations cover system development, but not explicit design for interoperability and reuse.

development area: Automation frameworks and workflow orchestration concepts
description: Knowledge of automation approaches, pipeline design, process orchestration, and rules-based processing to support automation-first system development.
historic work: Key Activities - Develops processing systems and applications used to manipulate, store and retrieve statistical data.
change to work: System development is no longer only about functional delivery; it must now be designed for reuse, automation, and integration from the beginning. Development work would need to conform to digital-by-default principles and avoid isolated or bespoke solutions where standard components exist.
justification: The role must embed automation as a core design principle rather than a later enhancement.

development area: Requirements engineering for interoperability and compliance
description: Ability to translate digital standards, integration requirements, and automation constraints into formal system, database, and testing specifications.
historic work: Key Activities - Designs specifications for the testing of data and for the maintenance and development of databases.
change to work: Specifications must now include proof of digital compliance, interoperability, and integration readiness, not only technical test conditions and maintenance needs. Database and testing specifications will need to support standardized interfaces, reusable components, and automation-friendly controls.
justification: Current specifications focus on testing and maintenance, but not explicit interoperability compliance or digital assurance requirements.

description: Knowledge of compliance checkpoints, approval evidence, and documentation expectations related to reuse, automation, interoperability, and exception handling.
historic work: Key Activities - Designs specifications for the testing of data and for the maintenance and development of databases.
change to work: Specifications must now include proof of digital compliance, interoperability, and integration readiness, not only technical test conditions and maintenance needs. Database and testing specifications will need to support standardized interfaces, reusable components, and automation-friendly controls.
justification: Future-state specification work requires structured evidence that solutions meet digital priorities before progressing.
